claims.text: HEAs have multi-principal-element compositions and a very large composition-selection space.
High-throughput computational screening with a data-driven or machine-learning model can rationally design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEA compositions.
Computational power and screening criteria mediate the proposed composition-design process.
High-throughput methods can rapidly screen large numbers of potential alloy compositions.
Density-functional-theory calculations or molecular-dynamics simulations can be used in the proposed screening process.
The screening process can identify an optimal HEA composition that is intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight.
Existing alloy-design approaches include thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations.
The proposed method is constrained by CPU/GPU capacity, memory, screening criteria, and database size.
A database size in the range of 1,000 to 100,000 is relevant to the proposed screening method.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality of the computational models.
Prediction accuracy depends on database size.
Failure of screened compositions to significantly outperform traditionally designed compositions would falsify the hypothesis.
